checkpoints.notes: 5 concepts brainstormed and scored (reviewed Cycle 1's concepts.md first to avoid duplicates); Orbit Duel: AI Rival selected (evolution of Cycle 1's Orbit Duel, adds single-player AI opponent + mode select, resolves a Cycle 1 follow-up), Echo Maze as runner-up/future-cycle candidate.

Produced via a dedicated Opus 5 subagent. Key decisions: intent-layer indirection (ship.intent booleans) so AI and human inputs share one physics path; phase state machine (menu/playing/gameover) replacing Cycle 1's boolean gameOver, with a backward-compatible getter; deterministic priority-arbitrated AI (evade > orbit > engage) with a reaction-delay latch as the difficulty knob; registerHit() extracted as the single scoring path so the win-condition E2E test exercises real logic; 12 new AI tunables with documented invariants; implementation ordered so the win-condition test (Cycle 1's top follow-up) is written before AI polish. Target file game/cycle2/index.html; game/index.html stays frozen.

Self-contained playable prototype per docs/cycle2/design.md: intent layer, menu/playing/gameover state machine, mode-select screen (1P vs AI / 2P local), deterministic priority-arbitrated AI (evade/orbit/engage), registerHit() extracted as the single scoring path, full window.__orbitDuel.test hook surface (setPaused/step/updateAI/registerHit/startMatch/toMenu). Verified game/index.html (Cycle 1) is byte-for-byte unchanged (git diff --quiet passes).

Automated Playwright/headless-Chromium tests, all PASS: T2 win-condition end-to-end (Cycle 1's top follow-up, now closed) for both modes; T1 regression against Cycle 1 behavior + audit guard that game/index.html is unmodified; T3 deterministic AI behavior (aim convergence, shooting, star evasion, 30s survivability soak with 0 deaths, fairness invariants, cross-run determinism) with one documented non-blocking soft-fail (AI didn't score on a target parked directly across the star from it -- expected per the design's deliberate no-gravity-lead-aim tradeoff, not a defect); T4 mode-select/navigation. One test-construction bug found and fixed during T3 authoring (arena screen-wrap made naive distance-to-star a misleading proxy after a long thrust run -- fixed by shortening the assertion window, not a game bug).
